summary: Session fingerprint rotation failure prevents access to internal console after network change
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:10 UTC a subset of employees were unable to access the Redwood Console after switching networks (e.g., from corporate VPN to home ISP). Users receive a generic 'Session mismatch' error and are forced to re-authenticate repeatedly. Impact: ~25% of internal staff observed interrupted access to internal dashboards, some lost active SSO-derived roles during the re-auth flow which blocked access to billing and oncall tools. Scope appears limited to employees who used IdP-initiated SSO or had long-lived sessions across network boundary changes.

Environment: Production, us-east, console-route behind auth-bridge v2.8.1, session-store: redis-cluster-3, Okta org: redwood-prod.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Sign into Console via Okta SSO and remain idle for >30m. 2) Change network (disconnect VPN, switch to home network). 3) Attempt action that requires elevated RBAC (open Billing or Oncall). 4) Observe 'Session mismatch' and forced re-auth. 5) After re-auth, some users are missing prior roles until a backfill occurs.

Relevant logs: auth-bridge logs show frequent 'fingerprint_mismatch' entries during network change window; session-store shows duplicate session keys with different cookie domains; Okta assertion logs show successful SAML assertion; no 5xx from console service.
steps_to_reproduce: Sign into Console via Okta SSO and remain idle for >30m
Switch network (VPN -> home ISP) or change client IP
Observe 'Session mismatch' error and repeated re-authentication prompt
logs: 2026-03-10T08:11:24Z auth-bridge[warn]: fingerprint_mismatch uid=ajenkins session=abc123 prev_ip=10.0.0.45 new_ip=52.3.12.9
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: stricter fingerprinting in auth-bridge v2.8.1 treats IP or cookie domain change as threat and invalidates session before Okta reassertion completes
Observed session-store containing duplicate keys with different cookie domains (redwood-internal.local vs redwood.local) starting after deployment at 2026-03-09 23:50 UTC
Reproduced locally by switching network interfaces; auth-bridge emits fingerprint_mismatch when only cookie domain differs, even when SAML assertion is presented immediately
Checked Redis cluster: TTLs look normal; no eviction events correlated with incident window
Cross-checked Okta logs: assertion success for affected users, so IdP not root cause
SRE ran a canary rollback of auth-bridge v2.8.1 to v2.8.0 in us-east at 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC — immediate reduction in fingerprint_mismatch alerts
comments: 2026-03-10 08:35 - Linh Tran (SRE): Observed spike in fingerprint_mismatch. Correlates with auth-bridge deploy 2026-03-09 23:50 UTC. Rolling back to v2.8.0 in canary zone now.
2026-03-10 09:05 - Marcus Chen (Auth Eng): Canary rollback performed. Error rate dropped ~90% for canary hosts. Still seeing residual user sessions failing due to stale cookie domains.

2026-03-10 11:12 - Diego Morales (Frontend): Users report losing RBAC roles after re-auth. Suspect session->user role bindings are stored separately and not being reattached on fresh SAML assertion unless session ID preserved.

2026-03-11 14:01 - Aisha Patel (IAM): Runbook step executed: global session invalidation (force sign-out) for affected user cohort to ensure fresh sessions with correct domain/cookie; instructed impacted teams to re-login.

2026-03-12 10:30 - Marcus Chen (Auth Eng): Mitigation complete: rolled back problematic change, invalidated sessions, deployed corrective patch to canonicalize cookie domain during rotation. Monitoring added to detect duplicate session keys. Planning postmortem and follow-up JIRA tasks.
root_cause_hypothesis: A change in auth-bridge v2.8.1 introduced stricter fingerprint checks combined with an inadvertent cookie-domain canonicalization change. When clients change network, the auth-bridge saw a different cookie domain / fingerprint and invalidated the session even as Okta re-asserted the user, leading to repeated re-auth and dropped RBAC bindings.
resolution: Mitigated: rolled back auth-bridge v2.8.1 to v2.8.0 in prod us-east, performed global session invalidation for impacted cohort, and released patch v2.8.2 that canonicalizes cookie domain on rotation and relaxes non-critical fingerprint components. Added metric 'auth.fingerprint_mismatch.count' and alert. Permanent: add canary gating for auth changes and an automated session repair job to reattach RBAC after successful SAML assertion.
follow_up_actions: INT-95345 - postmortem and timeline (owner: Marcus Chen)
INT-95346 - add canary gating + e2e test for session rotation across network changes (owner: Linh Tran)
INT-95347 - implement session repair job to reattach RBAC after SAML reassertion (owner: Diego Morales)
